title: Grep tool's -A/-B context output occasionally corrupts leading "//" to "\\"
details:
**What happened:** Grep with `-A`/`-B` context lines twice rendered a JS line comment's leading `//` as a single `\` character in the tool result (e.g. `      \ 2026-09-04: 드래그...` instead of `      // 2026-09-04: 드래그...`). A direct `Read` of the exact same line both times showed the correct `//`, confirming the file itself was fine and the corruption was in Grep's context-line rendering only.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model.
**Repro:** Ran Grep with `-A`/`-B` context spanning a line beginning with `      // comment text` inside a `<script>` block of a large (~9000 line) `.html` file; the affected line's leading `//` rendered as `\` in the returned context, while re-reading via `Read` (no grep context) showed it correctly.
**Evidence:** File `tools/dashboard.html` in project `AROS_Reverse_Eng_260803`, near line ~2560 and separately near line ~8963 (line numbers shifted across edits in the session) — same two-tool-output-vs-Read discrepancy pattern both times.
**Cause:** Not verified — root cause of the rendering corruption is unknown; only the symptom (Grep context vs Read mismatch) was confirmed.

This nearly caused a false bug report to the user (almost claimed their code had a stray backslash / syntax error based on Grep context output before double-checking with Read).
